entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This writ petition is directed against the order dated 10.01.2014 passed by the respondent No.2-Deputy Commissioner-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Ranchi in Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13, whereby and whereunder a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- was imposed upon the accused persons, as penalty, on account of the contravention of the provision of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Out of Rs.3,00,000/-, these two petitioners have been ordered to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- and the rest of Rs.2,50,000/- is to be paid by the accused No.3-Bihar State Milk Co-operative Federation.
It appears that the complainant-Food Safety Inspector, Ranchi collected 800 Grams of 'Paneer' from Hotel Ranchi Ashok for the purpose of its analysis.

The said sample was sent before the Analyst and after analysis, it was found that the batch number, which was put in over the packets of Paneer had been not written prominently and hence, it was not readable and, thereby, it was found to be misbranded in terms of provision as contained in Section 3(zf)(C)(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

On finding the product to be 'misbranded', a report was submitted before the respondent No.2-Deputy Commissioner-cum-AdjudicatingOfficer, Ranchi, who having found the appellants guilty for contravention of the provision of the said Act, awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- to be paid by the accused persons.
Out of it, an amount of Rs.50,000/- was ordered to be paid by these petitioners vide order dated 10.01.2014 passed in Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Being aggrieved with that order dated 10.01.2014, this writ petition has been filed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only point, which has been taken in this application is that while fixing the quantum of the amount of penalty, the respondent No.2 has never taken into account the factors, which have been enumerated in sub clause (a) to (e) of Section 49 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and thereby, on this ground alone, the impugned order suffers from illegality and is fit to be set aside by this Court.

There has been no dispute of the fact that packet of Paneer, which was collected from the Hotel Ashok, Ranchi, was found to be misbranded, in terms of provision as contained in Section 3(zf)(C)(i)
of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
On such accusation, the fine as aforesaid was imposed.

That order, according to learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, never happens to be in accordance with law, as the court, while awarding penalty, should have taken into account the factor which has been enumerated in sub clause (a) to (e) of Section 49 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 .

The said Section reads as follows:-
49. General provisions relating to penalty.- While adjudging the quantum of penalty under this Chapter, the Adjudicating Officer or the Tribunal, as the case may be, shall have due regard to the following:-
(a) the amount of gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the contravention,
(b) the amount of loss caused or likely to cause to any person as result of the contravention,
(c) the repetitive nature of the contravention,
(d) whether the contravention is without his knowledge, and (e) any other relevant factor.
From the perusal of the provision, as referred to above, it is evident that the Adjudicating Officer,
while awarding punishment, is required to give due consideration of the facts as aforesaid.

Here in the instant case, though it has been written in the order about the consideration of the factor relating to gain and unfair advantage, but the same appears to be mentioned only for the sake of mentioning as quantum of gain or unfair advantage never seems to have been quantified.

According to learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the court has never taken into account this aspect of the matter, as it is the case of the petitioner that only 10Kg of Paneer had been purchased and in that event, the petitioners cannot be said to have taken unfair advantage to the extent to which fine has been imposed even by consuming entire quantity of Paneer.

That apart, other factors also do not seem to have been given due regard by the Adjudicating Officer and, therefore, the order passed by the Adjudicating Officer, seems to be quite bad.

sentences.text: Accordingly, oder dated 10.01.2014, relating to quantum of fine amount is hereby, set aside.

H o w e v e r , t h e m a t t e r i s r e m a n d e d b a c k t o t h e r e s p o n d e n t N o . 2 - D e p u t y Commissioner-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Ranchi so that he may pass a fresh order in accordance with law, after taking into account the provision as contained in sub clause (a) to (e) of Section 49 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Accordingly, this writ petition is allowed.

(R.R. Prasad, J.) Ravi/
